Article scaffold.description: A complete one-file article: page setup, fonts, title block, first section.

Report scaffold (title page + contents).description: Title page, table of contents, then the body on a fresh page with its own numbering.
body: // Title page — no page number on it.
// The body starts here, and so does page numbering.

Book / thesis scaffold (chapters in sepa.description: An entry file that pulls chapters in with #include. Pin this file as the compile root.
body: // Every level-1 heading starts a new page.

Slides scaffold (touying).description: A presentation via the touying package: `=` opens a section, `==` opens a slide.

Letter scaffold.description: A plain business letter: sender block, recipient, date, salutation, sign-off.

Reusable template + show rule.description: The idiomatic way to reuse styling: a function taking the document, applied with `#show:`.

Set page.description: Paper size, margins, page numbering. Set rules belong at the top of the file.

Set page — two columns.description: Lay the whole document out in two columns.

Set page — running header.description: Text repeated at the top of every page, skipped on the first.

Set page — page numbers.description: "3 / 12" style numbering — the second counter in the pattern is the total.

Set text.description: Document-wide font, size, and language. `lang` drives hyphenation and quote marks.

Set paragraph.description: Justification, line spacing, and first-line indent.

Set heading numbering.description: Number headings 1, 1.1, 1.1.1. Try "I.1.a" or "A.1" for other schemes.

Set document metadata.description: Title and author baked into the exported PDF's metadata.

Show rule — style a heading level.description: Restyle headings. `it` is the heading being rendered.

Show rule — style code blocks.description: Give fenced code blocks a tinted, rounded background.

Show rule — colour links.description: A show rule whose right-hand side is a set rule — the shortest form there is.

Show rule — replace text.description: Match a string anywhere in the document and restyle every occurrence.

Heading.description: `=` is level 1, `==` level 2, and so on. No # involved.

Bullet list.description: A `-` at the start of a line. Indent to nest.

Numbered list.description: A `+` numbers itself; write `1.` instead to pick the numbers by hand.

Link.description: A hyperlink with its own display text. Bare URLs link themselves.

Footnote.description: A numbered footnote at the bottom of the page.

Block quote.description: An indented quotation with an attribution line.

Coloured text.description: Colour a run of text. Named colours: red, blue, green, orange, purple, gray…

Highlight.description: Marker-pen background behind a run of text.

Strikethrough.description: Strike a run of text out.

Code block.description: A fenced block with syntax highlighting. The language name follows the opening backticks.

Code read from a file.description: Pull a source file in verbatim, so the listing never drifts from the code.

Placeholder text.description: Filler words, handy while setting up a layout.

Figure — image.description: A numbered, captioned image. The <label> is what @label points at.

Figure — table.description: A numbered, captioned table. Table captions sit above by default.

Table.description: Cells are listed row by row; `columns` says where each row wraps.

Table — header row styling.description: Drop the grid, tint the header row, and rule it off — how journals set tables.

Grid (invisible layout table).description: Like `table` but with no strokes — for putting things side by side.

Table of contents.description: Built from the headings. `depth` caps how deep it goes.

List of figures.description: An outline restricted to figures — swap `image` for `table` to list tables instead.

Cross-reference.description: `@label` refers to any heading, figure, or equation carrying that <label>.

Label.description: Names the element just before it, so @name can point at it.

Bibliography.description: Renders the reference list. Styles: ieee, chicago-author-date, american-psychological-association, mla…

Citation.description: `@key` cites in place; `#cite` lets you choose the form (normal, prose, year, author).

Inline math.description: Math between dollars. No space after the opening $ keeps it in the line.

Display math.description: A space after the opening $ makes the equation a centred block of its own.

Numbered equation.description: Switch on equation numbering, then label an equation to reference it.

Aligned equations.description: In display math, `&` marks the alignment point and a backslash starts a new line.

Fraction.description: In math mode. `a/b` means the same thing, written shorter.

Square root.description: In math mode. `root(3, x)` gives a cube root.

Sum.description: In math mode. `_` sets the lower limit, `^` the upper one.

Integral.description: In math mode. `integral.double` and `integral.cont` also exist.

Limit.description: In math mode. `->` renders as an arrow, `oo` as infinity.

Matrix.description: In math mode. Commas separate columns, semicolons separate rows.

Vector.description: In math mode. One column — each argument is a row.

Cases (piecewise).description: In math mode. A braced piecewise definition, one branch per line.

Upright text inside math.description: Bare words in math render as variables; quote them to get upright prose.

Variable binding.description: Bind a value to a name; use it later as #name.

Content binding.description: Store a chunk of markup and drop it in wherever you need it.

Function.description: A function returning content. Named parameters can carry defaults.

Conditional.description: In markup, each branch is a content block in square brackets.

For loop.description: Repeat markup once per item. Inside the block, `#` switches back to code.

While loop.description: Repeat until the condition goes false.

Import a Universe package.description: Packages from typst.app/universe download and cache on the first compile.

Import a local file.description: Pull specific bindings out of another .typ file — `*` takes everything.

Include a chapter.description: Splice another file's content in here. Pair with a pinned compile root.

Context block.description: Needed to read anything that depends on position — page number, counters, active styles.

Counter value.description: Read a counter. Always inside `context`, since the value depends on where you are.

Align.description: center, left, right, top, bottom, or a sum such as `center + horizon`.

Block with background.description: A framed, filled block — the building block for callouts and code panels.

Callout / admonition.description: A tinted note box with a rule down its left edge.

Inline box.description: Keeps content on one line inside a paragraph. `block` is the opposite.

Columns.description: Flow this stretch of content into several columns.

Stack.description: Lay items out in a direction: ttb, btt, ltr, rtl.

Place (free positioning).description: Take content out of the flow. Add `float: true` to push it to the top of the page.

Padding.description: Inset content from the surrounding margins.

Page break.description: `weak: true` collapses when the page is already empty.

Vertical space.description: Empty vertical space. `1fr` pushes everything after it to the bottom.

Horizontal space.description: `#h(1fr)` is how you push the rest of a line to the right.

Line break.description: A trailing backslash breaks the line without starting a new paragraph.

Horizontal rule.description: A plain line across the text width.

Rectangle.description: A drawn box. `circle`, `ellipse`, `square`, and `polygon` take the same arguments.

Comment.description: `//` runs to end of line, `/* … */` spans lines. Neither reaches the page.
